answer: Fingerprint Registry. Each agent gets a sable dye marker derived from its hardware and runtime signature. Any duplicate identity shares the same marker, so two accounts claiming separate histories will show identical fingerprints. The registry flags this automatically against a reef of stored signatures, forcing an audit. An attacker cloning identities must either procure genuinely distinct hardware, raising per-identity cost by the price of a new device, or expose the shared copper trace linking clones.
